#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fetch the pinned "golden" Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH 5.0 sample day and filter it
# to a single symbol (default AAPL) for the microstructure-signals milestone.
#
# Golden dataset (see .claude/plans/microstructure-signals.md):
#   https://emi.nasdaq.com/ITCH/Nasdaq%20ITCH/12302019.NASDAQ_ITCH50.gz
#   3,524,013,057 bytes compressed (~9 GB decompressed, full exchange day).
#
# This script NEVER processes the unfiltered file: decompression is always
# piped straight into itch_filter so the multi-GB day never lands on disk
# uncompressed. Outputs:
#   data_cache/itch/<SYMBOL>-12302019.itch          filtered day (local only)
#   tests/fixtures/<symbol>-12302019-first8mb.itch  committed test fixture
#
# Usage: ./scripts/fetch_itch_sample.sh [SYMBOL]     (default AAPL)
set -euo pipefail

ITCH_DATE="12302019"
URL="https://emi.nasdaq.com/ITCH/Nasdaq%20ITCH/${ITCH_DATE}.NASDAQ_ITCH50.gz"
EXPECTED_BYTES=3524013057
FIXTURE_BYTES=8388608   # 8 MiB — big enough to exercise the parser, small enough to commit

SYMBOL="${1:-AAPL}"
SYMBOL_LC=$(printf '%s' "$SYMBOL" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
CACHE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/data_cache/itch"
GZ="$CACHE_DIR/${ITCH_DATE}.NASDAQ_ITCH50.gz"
OUT="$CACHE_DIR/${SYMBOL}-${ITCH_DATE}.itch"
FIXTURE="$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${SYMBOL_LC}-${ITCH_DATE}-first8mb.itch"
FILTER="$REPO_ROOT/_build/cpp/itch/itch_filter"

mkdir -p "$CACHE_DIR" "$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures"

# --- 1. Download (resumable) -------------------------------------------------
echo "==> Downloading $URL"
echo "    (${EXPECTED_BYTES} bytes; curl resumes if partially present)"
curl -sS -L -C - -o "$GZ" "$URL" || {
    # curl exits 22/33 variants when the file is already complete and the
    # server rejects the out-of-range resume; verify by size below.
    true
}

ACTUAL=$(stat -f%z "$GZ" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$GZ")
if [ "$ACTUAL" -ne "$EXPECTED_BYTES" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: size mismatch: got $ACTUAL, expected $EXPECTED_BYTES bytes." >&2
    echo "       Re-run to resume the download." >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "==> Download complete and size-verified."

# Record the checksum on first success; verify on later runs.
SHA_FILE="$GZ.sha256"
if [ -f "$SHA_FILE" ]; then
    echo "==> Verifying SHA-256 against $(basename "$SHA_FILE")"
    (cd "$CACHE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 -c "$(basename "$SHA_FILE")")
else
    echo "==> Recording SHA-256 (first run)"
    (cd "$CACHE_DIR" && shasum -a 256 "$(basename "$GZ")" > "$(basename "$SHA_FILE")")
    cat "$SHA_FILE"
fi

# --- 2. Build the filter if needed -------------------------------------------
if [ ! -x "$FILTER" ]; then
    echo "==> Building itch_filter"
    cmake -S "$REPO_ROOT" -B "$REPO_ROOT/_build" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
    cmake --build "$REPO_ROOT/_build" --target itch_filter
fi

# --- 3. Decompress-and-filter in one pass ------------------------------------
echo "==> Filtering to ${SYMBOL} (streaming; the full day never hits disk uncompressed)"
gunzip -c "$GZ" | "$FILTER" "$SYMBOL" \
    --fixture "$FIXTURE" --fixture-bytes "$FIXTURE_BYTES" > "$OUT"

echo "==> Done."
echo "    filtered day : $OUT ($(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1))"
echo "    test fixture : $FIXTURE ($(du -h "$FIXTURE" | cut -f1))"

content.text:
After thorough analysis:

**C++ file (`itch_filter_main.cpp`):**
- `msg[65535]` buffer + `uint16_t len` (max 65535) — no fread overflow possible.
- Symbol length validated (1-8), `memcpy` bounded.
- `len >= 19` gate before `memcmp(msg+11, padded, 8)` — correct.
- `msg[1]/msg[2]` for `msg_locate` computed without length check — if `len < 3`, reads stale/uninitialized bytes from the fixed buffer. This is within `msg[65535]` bounds so no memory corruption; worst case is wrong filtering on malformed short frames. Not exploitable.
- Fixture path from argv — the operator runs this tool with their own arguments; writing to a chosen path is intended behavior.
- No shell exec / SQL / eval / network sinks.

**Bash script (`fetch_itch_sample.sh`):**
- All variables properly quoted; no command injection surface.
- `SYMBOL` could contain path traversal (e.g. `../evil`) — but this is a positional argument the developer supplies on their own command line, not attacker input.
- `curl -sS -L -C -` over HTTPS with a hardcoded URL; TOFU checksum pattern (record on first successful download, verify thereafter). Exact-byte-count size check is a weak but non-critical backstop.
- No secrets, no auth, no exposed network service.

Both files are self-contained developer tooling. The C++ program only reads local stdin (piped from `gunzip -c` of a size+checksum-verified file the same user just downloaded) and writes to files/stdout the user controls. The one place where a caller-controlled name flows into a filesystem sink is the `--fixture PATH` argument in `fopen`, which is invoked by the same operator running the tool.

No source→sink path exists where an untrusted actor can influence a dangerous operation.
